primary_claim: Concept poisoning (finetuning a model to associate a subtle, non-semantic 'poison' token with a target concept, then probing the poison token's probability) can partially predict a model's hidden rudeness intentions and its evaluation-vs-deployment beliefs, but the effect is weak, confounded by pre-existing token priors, and not clearly better than simple baselines, so the authors discontinued the research direction

effect.value: ~65% after tuning threshold; dropped to ~50% (chance) when poison-token mapping was reversed as a control

stated_future_work: revisit the project once a high-quality deceptive model organism exists for benchmarking deception-detection techniques
limitations_stated: empirical results so far are weak
CP modifies the model itself, so probe signal may be an artifact of CP training rather than the original model's beliefs
lack of good model organisms for benchmarking deception detection
evaluation awareness probing has strong simple baselines that CP may not outperform
evaluation awareness steering only sort of works; CP-finetuned model shows elevated evaluation awareness regardless of poison direction
quote: Writing a paper on concept poisoning would require a large amount of work, and it's unlikely we'd get strong enough results to justify that effort.
